The moment Fortnite fans have been waiting for has officially arrived, and Epic Games has finally revealed the upcoming Fortnite Spider-Man Brand New Day collaboration skins. The trailer was officially shared on Sony and Fortnite channels, and it provided an exclusive look at Spider-Man: Brand New Day.Other major highlights of the trailer were the Punisher skin and the Web Shooters. It will be exciting to see all the new content arriving to the game very soon. In the section below, we take a look at everything revealed about Fortnite x Spider-Man Brand New Day.The new trailer posted by Fortnite has struck the fans with excitement and it commenced by providing a brief look at the new Spider-Man skin. The same is essentially based on Tom Holland's appearance in Spider-Man: Brand New Day.The trailer further featured a message from Tom Holland, and he talked about the addition of new outfits based on the upcoming movie. He also mentioned about the return of the Web Shooters, which has been one of the most awaited things.There were two major skin reveals as part of the Fortnite x Spider-Man Brand New Day trailer. The first being the Spider-Man skin based on the appearance of Tom Holland in the new movie.Aside from that, the iconic antihero Punisher has been confirmed to make his Fortnite debut.One of the finest aspects of the new trailer was the reveal of the Punisher skin that will be arriving to the battle royale experience.Essentially, the skin is going to be based on Jon Bernthal's look in the movie. The trailer further provided us with a glance at Punisher and Spider-Man fighting The Hulk in the streets of Battlewoods. Nevertheless, there has been no information about a Hulk skin releasing.The return of the Mythic Web Shooters is arguably the most exciting gameplay development in the entire reveal. After the exclusive look at Spider-Man: Brand New Day, the trailer provided the first glance at the Web Shooters back in action.Adding to the excitement, Epic has revealed that the upcoming Web Shooters Power Hours on August 1, 2026, will feature unlimited Web Shooters for players to use.The leaked Fortnite Spider-Man Sprite was not revealed during the trailer. As a result, there is a chance that the developers could be waiting to reveal it later on. Nevertheless, the same is not confirmed, and you will have to wait for further announcements.Fortnite x Spider-Man Brand New Day skins and related content will be introduced to the battle royale experience after the release of v41.30. The same is set to arrive on July 30, 2026, at 4 AM ET, which falls in line with the release of Spider-Man Brand New Day.The Fortnite x Spider-Man Brand New Day collaboration is shaping up to be one of the biggest crossover events of Chapter 7 Season 3.
Article Summary: The Fortnite x Spider-Man Brand New Day trailer has been released. The trailer was officially shared on Sony and Fortnites channels. It provided an exclusive look at the upcoming movie. Other major highlights of the trailer were the Punisher skin and the Web Shooters.

Article Title: Watch: Disturbing footage captures the moments after Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy's son Elijah was taken into custody following Mia's shooting
Article Text:
Chilling footage captures the moments after Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy's son Elijah was taken into custody following Mia's shooting(Image Via Getty)

New footage shows the tense police response after Elijah Bieniemy's arrest

Newly released bodycam footage has revealed the tense police response that followed the shooting involving Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy's family. The video, obtained and published by ABC 7 News, shows officers arriving at the scene, securing the home and taking Bieniemy's 27-year-old son, Elijah Bieniemy, into custody. While the footage does not show the shooting itself, it provides the clearest look yet at the chaotic moments that unfolded immediately afterward.The release of the video comes days after authorities confirmed that Mia Bieniemy, Eric Bieniemy's wife, survived the shooting after suffering gunshot wounds to her arm and chest. She remains in stable condition, while investigators continue working to determine what led to the incident.The bodycam footage runs for roughly four and a half minutes and begins with multiple officers arriving at what appears to be the Bieniemy family residence. Dressed in tactical gear and carrying rifles, officers carefully surround the entrance before making their way inside the home.After that, Elijah Bieniemy is seen outside in handcuffs as officers secure the area. The video then captures an ambulance arriving at the scene before paramedics wheel a stretcher into the residence.A short time later, emergency crews escort Mia Bieniemy out for medical treatment while officers continue locking down the neighborhood. The footage ends with investigators placing crime scene tape around the property as they begin collecting evidence.Authorities have since charged Elijah Bieniemy with malicious wounding, use of a firearm in the commission of a felony and discharging a firearm inside an occupied dwelling. Investigators have not released details about what may have led to the shooting, and the investigation remains active.The tragedy also brought immediate changes for the Kansas City Chiefs. Eric Bieniemy left training camp to be with his family, forcing the team to make a temporary coaching adjustment just weeks before the NFL season.Chiefs head coach Andy Reid addressed the situation during his post-practice press conference on July 27. Speaking to reporters after Bieniemy's departure from camp, Reid acknowledged the difficult circumstances facing his longtime assistant.He said, "Things happen. You just got to work through it, and that's where we're at right now. Time will have to be involved in this to help heal a little bit, but it'll all work out in the long run."With Bieniemy away from the team, Kansas City promoted pass game coordinator Joe Bleymaier to handle offensive coordinator duties on an interim basis. Reid stressed that the Chiefs fully support Bieniemy during this difficult period, with football taking a back seat as his family deals with the aftermath of the shooting. As of now, Mia is in stable condition.Currently, the newly released bodycam footage answers some questions about what happened after police reached the scene. At the same time, it also highlights just how quickly the situation unfolded. As the legal process moves forward and investigators continue gathering evidence, the focus remains on Mia Bieniemy's recovery and on the family at the center of one of the NFL's most heartbreaking stories of the offseason.
Article Summary: New footage shows the tense police response after Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy's son Elijah was taken into custody following his wife's shooting. The video, obtained and published by ABC 7 News, shows officers arriving at the scene, securing the home and taking Elijah into custody. Authorities have since charged Elijah with malicious wounding, use of a firearm in the commission of a felony and discharging a firearm inside an occupied dwelling. The release of the video comes days after authorities confirmed that Mia Bien iemy survived the shooting. She remains in stable condition.

Article Title: "Whatever I give her, it will never equal what she gave me": How Lamine Yamal refused to blame his mother despite childhood struggles that changed his life forever
Article Text:
Lamine Yamal's heartfelt words about his mother (Getty Images)

Why does Lamine Yamal say he has nothing to blame his mother for despite a difficult childhood?

What did Lamine Yamal say about his football style and his unexpected rise at Barcelona?

Lamine Yamal has just lifted the FIFA World Cup at 19. He celebrated with a postal code gesture, the number 304 flashed to a global audience, a quiet nod to Rocafonda, the working-class Mataró neighbourhood that raised him. Behind that celebration sits a story most football coverage has barely scratched. His mother, Sheila Ebana, had him at 16, raised him in a flat where the bedroom and kitchen shared the same walls, and worked restaurant shifts to buy him a PlayStation she could barely afford. Yamal has not forgotten a single detail.Sheila Ebana emigrated from Bata, Equatorial Guinea to Catalonia as a teenager. She became a mother at 16 while still figuring out life in a country that was not her own. She and Mounir Nasraoui separated when Lamine was three, and she chose to stay in Granollers rather than uproot him again. She kept working. She kept showing up.Yamal spoke about this directly, and without any self-pity: "I may not have had the best childhood in the world, but she made me see only the beautiful side and enjoy life. I have nothing to blame her for."That is not a polished media line. That is a 19-year-old who genuinely remembers what it felt like when his mother came home after a restaurant shift, sat with him, made food, and went back to work.He remembers the PlayStation she bought him despite how little they had. He remembers the holidays that somehow felt full.He put it plainly in a separate interview: "Whatever I give her, it will never equal what she gave me. My mother was one of my role models when I was young."The media tends to focus on Mounir Nasraoui, Yamal's father, who is loud, visible, and never misses a match. Sheila has largely stayed out of the spotlight. But inside Yamal's own telling of his story, she is the central figure. The DAZN documentary '304' makes that clear. So does every interview where he talks about his early years.When Yamal moved to La Masia at 12, Sheila stayed behind in Granollers. She kept working. She kept her life small so his could grow large. That kind of sacrifice does not get a trophy. It rarely even gets acknowledged. But Yamal acknowledges it every time someone puts a microphone near him.Before La Masia, Lamine Yamal played his first football at La Torreta, a local club near Rocafonda. The style he built there, direct, unpredictable, joy-driven, is the same one that now tortures full-backs at the highest level.He described himself in the Decoded documentary with a straightforwardness that feels almost disarming: "I'm a creative and entertaining player. I might go long minutes without touching the ball, but in a single minute I can make you enjoy watching a football match."That self-awareness matters. Plenty of teenage prodigies talk about the game in broad, rehearsed terms. Yamal understands what he actually does on a pitch and why it works. He knows his minutes of quiet are not absence; they are positioning for something decisive.He also admitted that even he did not see the Barcelona first team coming so soon: "I could imagine that I might play for Barcelona, but never this quickly. It's a dream, because from a young age you dream of playing Champions League matches."His rise has moved so fast he has rarely had the chance to absorb it. "Everything happens so fast that you don't fully think about it," he said. "Thank God, I haven't suffered any serious injury, but there are moments when you say: what a beautiful experience, because this is something anyone would wish for."Now, at 19, Sheila watches her son celebrate World Cup wins on the biggest stages in the sport. She has 200,000 followers on Instagram and around 1.5 million on TikTok. On his 18th birthday, she posted a video that said everything a mother could say: that no matter how much he grows, he will always be her little child. Yamal's response was to keep telling the world exactly who built him.
Article Summary: Lamine Yamal has just lifted the FIFA World Cup at 19. Behind that celebration sits a story most football coverage has barely scratched. His mother, Sheila Ebana, had him at 16, raised him in a flat where the bedroom and kitchen shared the same walls. She worked restaurant shifts to buy him a PlayStation she could barely afford. She kept her life small so his could grow large.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “When I was younger they were my driving force” - How Usain Bolt turned family sacrifice into sprinting greatness
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “When I was younger they were my driving force” - How Usain Bolt turned family sacrifice into sprinting greatness (Image via Getty)

How did Wellesley Bolt and Jennifer Bolt shape Usain Bolt’s career

Why did Usain Bolt’s parents stay in Sherwood Content after his success

What promise did Usain Bolt make after Wellesley Bolt’s passing

Why does Usain Bolt’s family story still inspire people around the world

Usain Bolt is remembered as the fastest man in history, but his journey began far from packed Olympic stadiums. Long before he became an eight-time Olympic gold medalist and world record holder, he was a young boy in Sherwood Content, Jamaica, who often preferred playing video games over attending track practice. Behind every milestone in his career stood his parents, Wellesley and Jennifer Bolt, whose discipline, sacrifices and support helped shape his future. Even after becoming one of the biggest names in sports, Bolt never forgot the people who believed in him first. Their influence remained a constant through his biggest victories and his hardest personal moments.Usain Bolt grew up in that small, rural community of Sherwood Content, in Trelawny Jamaica. His parents ran a local grocery shop, and at the same time they worked hard to provide for the family. Life was simple, and money was pretty limited, but they still made sure their children understood the real value of discipline along with hard work.Bolt had incredible natural speed from a young age. But staying focused was not always easy. He often tried to skip training so he could spend time playing video games with friends in nearby Falmouth.His father, Wellesley Bolt, refused to let that talent go to waste. He kept pushing his son to stay committed, while his mother, Jennifer Bolt, gave him the encouragement and emotional support he needed whenever things became difficult.Looking back at those early years, Bolt once said:“When I was younger they were my driving force. I was more focused on doing it for my country and my parents… From then on I was more careful and I sacrificed more. I wanted to use my talent in the right way.”As Bolt’s career reached new heights, he broke the world records in the 100 metres (9.58 seconds) and 200 metres (19.19 seconds) while becoming one of the most recognised athletes in the world.Despite his global fame and success, his parents chose not to leave their hometown. They continued living in Sherwood Content, and his father remained connected to the family’s local grocery shop instead of moving into a more luxurious life.That strong connection to home helped Bolt stay grounded during the biggest moments of his career. Whenever pressure built before major championships, his mother knew exactly how to calm him.Bolt recalled one conversation that stayed with him before an important race:“My mum randomly called me and said, ‘Are you OK?’ She said God told her to call me. ‘Don’t worry,’ she said, ‘You’ll be fine.’”Those simple words became another reminder that, even at the highest level of sport, family remained his biggest source of strength.In May 2025, Bolt lost his father, Wellesley Bolt. It was one of the most emotional moments of his life.While speaking before family and members of his community, he made a heartfelt promise to his mother, Jennifer Bolt. He said he would always be there for her.Bolt said:“Mom, just know that I’m here for you-fully. I’m not your husband, but I’m your child. You’re going to see more of me now than ever.”He later repeated that promise in just a few words:“Mom I got you.”The message reflected the same family values his parents had taught him throughout his life.People often remember Bolt for his Olympic medals, world records and unforgettable celebrations on the track. But his personal story shows that success was never built on talent alone.His parents handed him discipline, belief, and steady support long before the world even knew his name. Bolt has kept recognizing their part throughout his career, and he always talks with pride about where he’s from in Jamaica.His journey kind of nudges people toward the idea that accomplishments feel even heavier when they’re shared with family, the same unit that stood beside you from the start. For Bolt, the big lesson wasn’t only, running quicker than everyone else- no, it was more like never losing sight of where he came from, and also the people who helped him reach that point in the first place.
Article Summary: Usain Bolt grew up in Sherwood Content, Jamaica. His parents, Wellesley and Jennifer Bolt, ran a local grocery shop. Their discipline, sacrifices and support helped shape Bolt's future. Even after becoming one of the biggest names in sports, Bolt never forgot his parents.

NEW DELHI: India added more medals and strengthened its campaign at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow on Day 6, thanks to a historic silver from Gulveer Singh, another podium finish in weightlifting, and a strong showing in boxing.Gulveer was the standout performer, becoming the first Indian ever to win a medal in the men's 10,000m at the Commonwealth Games. The Army runner clocked 27:49.78 and stayed with the leaders throughout before finishing second behind Australia's Ky Robinson with a strong final-lap sprint.Harjinder Kaur also impressed by winning silver in the women's 69kg weightlifting event with a career-best total of 227kg (101kg snatch and 126kg clean and jerk).She also broke the Commonwealth Games snatch record twice and improved on the bronze medal she won at Birmingham 2022.India's boxers continued their fine run as Mandengbam Jadumani Singh (55kg), Preeti Pawar (54kg) and Priya Ghanghas (60kg) reached the semifinals, guaranteeing at least bronze medals.Priya recovered after losing the opening round of her quarterfinal to stay in the hunt for gold. However, Parveen Hooda and Kapil Pokhariya were knocked out in the quarterfinals.Vishal TK qualified for the men's 400m semifinals, while Rajesh Ramesh and high jumper Pooja Singh missed out. Weightlifter Nirupama Devi Seram registered no result after failing all her clean and jerk attempts.Swimmer Srihari Nataraj narrowly missed the 100m backstroke final, while Sajan Prakash failed to advance in the 50m butterfly.In para swimming, Karthik Budigina and Ali Imam finished sixth and eighth, respectively, in the S13 50m freestyle final. India also won its men's pairs bowls match, while Nayanmoni Saikia lost in the women's singles.At the end of Day 6, India were ninth in the medal standings with 12 medals, including two gold, seven silver and three bronze, while Australia remained on top with 80 medals.

Bron Breakker has quickly become one of WWE ’s biggest young stars, but long before he was hitting those powerful spears and collecting championships, the Rechsteiner family had already made a noticeable mark in professional wrestling. While Breakker has shaped his own identity inside the ring, his momentum and success are still closely tied to a family that has influenced the sport for decades.Bron grew up around people who contributed to his athletic career and mindset, from a WWE Hall of Fame father to a legendary uncle and a mother who instilled a strong work ethic. Here’s a closer look at the family behind one of WWE’s brightest stars.Bron Breakker, whose real name is Bronson Rechsteiner, was born on October 24, 1997, in Woodstock, Georgia. He is the youngest son of Rick Steiner and Jayme McKenzie.His father, Rick Steiner, is one of the most respected names in wrestling history. Fans better know him as the “Dog-Faced Gremlin.” Rick built an outstanding career across WCW, WWE and several other promotions. With his younger brother Scott Steiner, he helped form the Steiner Brothers, a legendary tag team that many people still call one of the best in the whole business.Bron has often talked about how much influence his father had on him. Rather than celebrating every success, Rick constantly challenged his son to do better, which mindset helped Bron get ready for a career in professional sports.Meanwhile, his mother, Jayme McKenzie, stayed away from the wrestling spotlight, but she still mattered a lot. She played an equally big role in raising Bron and his brothers. A former softball player at Oklahoma State, she encouraged all three of her sons to stay engaged in sports, and has been credited by Bron for teaching him discipline and hard work.Long before Bron Breakker entered WWE, the Steiner name had already become famous around the world. Rick and Scott Steiner dominated tag team wrestling during the late 1980s and 1990s, winning championships in WWE, WCW, NJPW and several other promotions.Rick became known for his powerful amateur wrestling style and signature moves like the Steiner Line and Steiner Driver. Scott later rebranded himself as “Big Poppa Pump,” turned into one of WCW’s biggest stars, and eventually won the WCW World Heavyweight Championship. Their success earned them induction into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2022.Even today, the Steiner Brothers are remembered as one of the greatest tag teams in wrestling history because of their mix of strength, athletic ability and unforgettable in-ring chemistry.Unlike his father and uncle, Bron Breakker did not begin his career in professional wrestling. His first dream was football, and he spent years developing as a football player before signing with the Baltimore Ravens as an undrafted free agent in 2020. Although his NFL opportunity was short-lived, it became the turning point that led him toward WWE.Breakker joined WWE in 2021 with no professional wrestling experience. Because of his athletic background, and his natural ability, he became one of NXT’s top stars. A lot of people expected him to step in under the well-known Steiner name, but Bron decided to build his own identity as “Bron Breakker.” That choice seems to be working, because he’s already established himself as one of WWE’s more promising young talents, while also keeping the family’s wrestling tradition in his own way.
Article Summary: Bron Breakker is the youngest son of Rick Steiner and Jayme McKenzie. His father, Rick, is one of the most respected names in wrestling history. With his younger brother Scott Steiner, he helped form the Steiner Brothers, a legendary tag team.

Deebo Samuel remains a free agent with training camps already open across the league, but the silence around his market may not last much longer. Fresh reporting from CBS Sports' Jordan Dajani has named several teams circling the veteran wideout, with one AFC squad emerging as the most talked-about fit in recent days. Here's everything currently known about where the former All-Pro could end up.The Raiders have previously emerged as one of the more frequently mentioned fits. Las Vegas enters the season with a young, relatively unproven receiving corps behind 25-year-old Tre Tucker, and analysts have pointed to Samuel's physical, YAC-heavy style as a natural complement whether it's veteran Kirk Cousins or rookie Fernando Mendoza under center. His thicker frame is seen as a nice pairing with the smaller, speedier Tucker and Jalen Nailor.But the Rams, now gaining momentum, were specifically named by CBS Sports as a fit if San Francisco (Samuel's original team) has no interest in a reunion.Sean McVay's offense already features Puka Nacua and Davante Adams catching passes from reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, but the idea is that Samuel wouldn't need to be a featured piece, just a versatile chess piece for reverses and third-and-short situations.Cincinnati, Indianapolis, and the Chargers round out the broader list of potential suitors, though those conversations appear less advanced.Unlike some free agents whose markets stall due to injury or off-field concerns, Samuel's situation seems to be more about roster fit and timing than any red flags. He was a captain in San Francisco and, by most accounts, an excellent locker room presence during his lone season in Washington.At 30 years old, some teams may simply be waiting to see how camp battles shake out before committing to a veteran addition, and Samuel himself has acknowledged the free agency wait has been "tough," describing the daily routine of checking his phone for word from his agent.No specific contract demands have been reported. As an outright free agent rather than a trade candidate, any team that signs Samuel would owe nothing in draft compensation, making him a relatively low-risk depth or rotational addition for a receiver room that needs seasoning.If Las Vegas is indeed the frontrunner, Samuel would slot in as a veteran security blanket rather than a true WR1, giving whoever starts at quarterback a reliable, savvy target who can win after the catch. For a Raiders offense looking to develop young talent around Tucker and Nailor, adding a proven veteran like Samuel even at this stage of his career could provide both production and a steadying presence in the room.Nothing is finalized, and no deal has been reported. But with camps underway and Samuel insisting he's "overly prepared" for his next opportunity, a decision could come sooner rather than later, and right now, the Raiders and Rams are the two names generating the most buzz.
Article Summary: Deebo Samuel remains a free agent with training camps already open across the league. CBS Sports' Jordan Dajani has named several teams circling the veteran wideout, with one AFC squad emerging as the most talked-about fit. As an outright free agent, any team that signs Samuel would owe nothing in draft compensation.

Article Title: “Talk to your parents”: Hamilton High School football player Khadyn Perkins dies by suicide as coach Elijah Asante shares heartfelt message
Article Text:
Khadyn Perkins and Elijah Asante (Image Via Getty)

Hamilton High School football community grieves as coach Elijah Asante pays tribute to Khadyn Perkins

Elijah Asante tells young athletes they are more important than football

The Hamilton High School community is mourning the loss of former football player Khadyn Perkins after the 19-year-old died by suicide on July 21 in San Pedro, California. Days after the tragedy, head coach Elijah Asante shared an emotional message asking young people to reach out when life feels overwhelming. He reminded his players that their lives matter far more than any game and that they never have to face difficult moments alone. The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner ruled Perkins’ death a suicide caused by traumatic injuries, with probable drowning listed as a contributing factor.Khadyn Perkins was a wide receiver and cornerback for Alexander Hamilton High School’s varsity football team in Los Angeles. He graduated in 2025 and proudly wore jersey No. 16 while playing in the CIF Los Angeles City Section Western League.According to the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner, Perkins died after jumping from a cliff near Sunken City in San Pedro on July 21. His death was officially ruled a suicide. The report listed traumatic injuries as the cause of death, while probable drowning was named as a contributing factor.The Los Angeles Fire Department responded to the area around 6:24 p.m.after receiving reports of a person in the water. Firefighters later found Perkins at the bottom of a cliff above the ocean near 500 West Paseo Del Mar. He was pronounced dead at the scene.Perkins’ death deeply affected teammates, coaches and everyone connected to Hamilton High School. Coach Elijah Asante, who returned from retirement in 2024 to rebuild the school’s football program, chose to speak directly to young athletes instead of focusing only on the loss.Following Perkins’ death, Elijah Asante shared a heartfelt message on social media, encouraging students to ask for help instead of struggling by themselves.“When life gets heavy, don’t carry it alone. Talk to your parents, talk to your coaches, talk to your teachers, talk to your teammates. There is strength and courage in asking for help. You are more important than football. You are more important than your sport. You are more important than any game, any score, or any expectation placed on you.”He also reminded young people that painful moments do not last forever.“Your future is greater than your current pain. You won’t even remember some of the things you struggle with now in the future. There are people who love you, believe in you, and will fight for you, even on the days when you don’t feel like fighting for yourself.”Asante’s words quickly became the focus of the conversation after Perkins’ death because they spoke about something much bigger than sports. His message urged students to lean on family, friends, teachers and coaches whenever life feels too difficult to handle alone.For many in the Hamilton High School community, the loss of Khadyn Perkins has become a painful reminder that mental health deserves the same attention as success on the field.

The 19-year-old died after jumping from a cliff near Sunken City in San Pedro on July 21. The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner ruled Perkins’ death a suicide caused by traumatic injuries, with probable drowning listed as a contributing factor. Coach Elijah Asante shared an emotional message asking young people to reach out when life feels overwhelming.

Why are officials not revealing more about Kyle Shanahan's car accident?

Kyle Shanahan's absence has become one of the biggest storylines as the San Francisco 49ers opened training camp, but not because of football. The head coach is recovering from serious injuries suffered in a car crash earlier this month, leaving the organisation without its leader during an important stage of pre-season preparations. While the team has disclosed the extent of Shanahan's injuries, several details surrounding the accident remain undisclosed, adding fresh questions as the 49ers balance optimism over his recovery with uncertainty over when he can fully return.The 49ers confirmed that the accident took place on July 14, 2026, near Shanahan's home in Los Altos Hills, California. Article Title: Why was Isaiah Rider arrested? Former Lakers star is in police custody in a case related to his wife Vanessa
Article Text:
Isaiah Rider. Image via: Getty Images

Former NBA champion Isaiah Rider arrested, again

What happened to Isaiah Rider?

Is Isaiah Rider's latest arrest related to his wife Vanessa?

Isaiah Rider was arrested again Thursday night, his third arrest in less than two months, this time on a misdemeanor charge for failing to comply with a court order. Maricopa County jail records show the former NBA Slam Dunk champion was booked Friday morning, pleaded guilty, and is expected to remain in custody until Tuesday.The charge traces back to a protective order his estranged wife, Vanessa, obtained last year. Rider, 55, has now been arrested twice before in connection with that same order, and the latest booking keeps a messy divorce and custody dispute firmly in public view.This is not new territory for Rider. He was picked up twice in December, first for allegedly violating the protective order and then again days later for skipping a hearing on whether that order should stay in place.A judge extended it after Vanessa showed up and Rider did not.Thursday's arrest follows the same pattern, a court-related misdemeanor rather than a new allegation of contact or violence, per TMZ . Police records describe it simply as a failure to comply with a court order, and the guilty finding suggests Rider did not contest it once he was in front of a judge.The former fifth overall pick in the 1993 NBA Draft spent nine seasons in the league, three years apiece with the Minnesota Timberwolves and Portland Trail Blazers before single seasons with the Atlanta Hawks, Los Angeles Lakers and Denver Nuggets.He won the Slam Dunk Contest as a rookie in 1994 and picked up a championship ring in 2001, even though he did not make the Lakers' playoff roster that year.The trouble began last year when Vanessa filed for a protective order, alleging Rider had been hostile toward her on multiple occasions. Court documents describe threatening language directed at her and their teenage son. Rider has denied the allegations and pointed instead to the timing of his own divorce filing in November 2024, arguing the order followed shortly after he moved to end the marriage.The order barred Rider from contacting Vanessa or their son and from going near the family home or the boy's school. Rider has claimed in filings that he did not receive the paperwork until December, weeks after it was granted in July.He was arrested that same month for allegedly violating the order, then arrested again for missing the hearing on whether it should be extended. Vanessa appeared for that hearing. The judge sided with her and kept the order in place, setting up the conditions that led to Thursday's arrest.Yes, at least indirectly. Thursday's booking was not for a new incident involving Vanessa but for failing to comply with a court order that exists because of her original petition, which makes this arrest part of the same unresolved case rather than a separate legal matter.Vanessa has been consistent about her reasons for seeking the order in the first place. "The Order of Protection was sought and granted solely for safety reasons, to protect myself and my child from further harm," she said in a statement , adding that she views the process as necessary rather than tactical and has asked the public to respect the privacy of a case involving a minor.
Article Summary: Isaiah Rider was arrested again Thursday night, this time on a misdemeanor charge for failing to comply with a court order. The charge traces back to a protective order his estranged wife, Vanessa, obtained last year. Rider, 55, has now been arrested twice before in connection with that same order.

How did Rafael Nadal overcome a career-threatening foot condition?

Why did Rafael Nadal always choose family and home over fame?

What did Rafael Nadal say about his wife and family during his injury battles?

What life lesson did Rafael Nadal learn from pain and defeat?

For years, Rafael Nadal inspired fans with his fight on the tennis court. What many people did not see was the battle he fought away from the spotlight. Long before becoming a 22-time Grand Slam champion, Nadal was told that a rare foot condition could end his career. He dealt with constant pain, serious injuries and doubts about whether he could keep playing. Yet he kept coming back. While his determination made headlines, Nadal has always said his biggest strength was the people who stood beside him. Their support helped him survive the hardest moments and build one of the greatest careers in tennis history.In 2005, Nadal won his first French Open title at just 19 years old. Soon after that breakthrough, he was diagnosed with Mueller-Weiss syndrome, a rare condition that affects the bones in the foot. Doctors warned that continuing his career at the highest level might not be possible.Instead of giving up, Nadal returned home to Manacor in Mallorca. There, he was surrounded by his father Sebastián, mother Ana María, sister Maribel and his longtime partner Mery Perelló. Their support gave him the strength to keep moving forward when his future looked uncertain.Looking back on those difficult years, Nadal once said:“Without the people that I have around me, all these years, without my family, without my team, it would be impossible.They give me peace of mind.”Despite becoming one of the biggest names in world sport, Nadal never left the place where he grew up. He stayed close to his family in Manacor and continued living the simple life that had shaped him from childhood.His uncle and longtime coach Toni Nadal taught him to stay humble, respect opponents and never believe he was bigger than the game. Those lessons stayed with him throughout his career.Rafael Nadal has often explained that returning home helped him switch off from the pressure of professional tennis. In Manacor, he was simply Rafa, spending time with friends and family. That normal life became an important part of maintaining his mental balance through the highs and lows of the sport.Nadal’s wife, Mery “Xisca” Perelló, was by his side long before he became a global star. She witnessed every comeback, every rehabilitation session and every painful setback that fans rarely saw.As injuries continued in the final years of his career, those shared sacrifices became even more meaningful. With his wife, young son and team watching from the stands, Nadal reflected on everything they had gone through together.He said:“Having my family here, my wife, my son, my team… it’s emotional because they know how hard the process has been. They have been through the good moments, but especially the tough moments during all these years of injuries.”Nadal never believed success came without suffering. Throughout his career, he played through injuries, long matches and physical pain that would have stopped many athletes. Instead of running from those challenges, he accepted them as part of the journey.That mindset became one of the biggest reasons behind his remarkable career.As Nadal explained:“If you don’t lose, you cannot enjoy the victories. You have to accept both things. I learned during my career to enjoy suffering.”His story goes far beyond Grand Slam trophies or records. It shows that true strength is not only about winning titles but also about staying grounded when life becomes difficult. Through every injury and every comeback, Nadal never lost sight of the people who mattered most. Their love gave him the peace, confidence and support to keep chasing his dreams, making his journey one of the most inspiring stories in modern sport.
Article Summary: Rafael Nadal was diagnosed with a career-threatening foot condition in 2005. Doctors told him it could end his career, but he refused to give up. Instead of giving up, Nadal returned home to Manacor in Mallorca. There, he was surrounded by his father, mother and sister. Their support gave him the strength to keep moving forward when his future looked uncertain.

Article Title: Archaeologists uncover rare 2,000-year-old Liubo game boards in Han Dynasty tombs, but its rules remain one of history's greatest mysteries
Article Text:
Image: AI Generated

Rare Liubo game boards discovered inside Han Dynasty tombs

What was Liubo, and why are its rules still unknown

Archaeology suggests Liubo was played at banquets as well as in tombs

Why Liubo remains one of archaeology's greatest unsolved puzzles

Centuries before chess spread across Asia, another board game captivated people throughout ancient China. Known as Liubo, it was played by emperors, nobles and ordinary families during the Han Dynasty, appearing so frequently that complete game sets were buried alongside the dead. Yet despite its popularity more than 2,000 years ago, the game's rules have almost entirely vanished. A recent archaeological discovery of rare Liubo game boards carved into Han Dynasty tombs has renewed interest in one of China's greatest historical mysteries. The find not only highlights the game's importance in everyday life and burial traditions but also underscores a remarkable paradox: archaeologists know what the board looked like, what pieces players used and where the game was played, yet no one can say with certainty how a match actually unfolded.Archaeologists identified two Liubo boards engraved directly onto square bricks inside Han Dynasty tombs dating to around 2,000 years ago. The discovery formed part of a larger excavation that also revealed pottery figurines, ceramic vessels and other funerary objects.Although Liubo boards have been discovered before, archaeologists rarely find them preserved in their original burial context. Their placement inside tombs suggests the game held lasting significance beyond recreation.During the Han Dynasty (206 BCE–220 CE), objects interred with the deceased often reflected activities or possessions considered valuable in the afterlife.Evidence from the Metropolitan Museum of Art supports this interpretation. Its well-preserved Liubo Board and Pieces, dating from the 1st century BCE–1st century CE, includes gaming pieces made from earthenware and bone. The museum notes that Liubo was "a popular game in the Han dynasty" and that such sets embodied wishes for the continuation of life after death.Liubo emerged no later than the Warring States period and remained one of China's most widely played board games for several centuries before gradually disappearing after the Han Dynasty.Players competed on a square board decorated with a distinctive TLV pattern, using gaming pieces and throwing six casting sticks or, in some versions, dice, to determine movement. Beyond these basic elements, certainty quickly disappears.In his influential study, ‘ A Tricky Game: A Re-evaluation of Liubo Based on Archaeological and Textual Evidence ,’ Dr Armin Selbitschka of Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich argues that modern scholarship has often overstated the game's supposed mystical or divinatory nature. After examining archaeological discoveries alongside surviving historical texts, he concludes that Liubo was primarily a game of entertainment, even though symbolic and religious associations emerged in certain regions during the later Eastern Han period.Crucially, no ancient instruction manual explaining the rules has survived. Historians have proposed several reconstructions based on excavated boards, gaming pieces and literary references, but none has achieved scholarly consensus. As a result, Liubo remains one of the few major ancient board games whose equipment is well documented while its gameplay remains largely unknown.The new discovery fits a broader archaeological pattern seen across Han Dynasty China. Selbitschka's research examined dozens of excavated tombs containing Liubo equipment and found that game boards frequently appeared alongside food vessels, drinking cups, musical instruments and figurines. Rather than representing isolated ritual objects, these groupings resemble scenes of banquets and social gatherings recreated inside tombs.The study argues that Liubo occupied an important place in elite entertainment. Historical writings by authors such as Sima Qian also refer to the game in descriptions of court life, competitions and leisure, reinforcing archaeological evidence that it was a familiar pastime rather than an obscure ceremonial practice.This interpretation contrasts with older theories that viewed Liubo mainly as a tool for divination because of the board's distinctive TLV design. According to Selbitschka, archaeological evidence indicates that recreational play remained its principal role throughout most of the Western Han period.Few ancient games present such an unusual challenge to historians. Archaeologists have uncovered exquisitely crafted lacquered boards, ceramic playing pieces, bronze fittings, carved stone examples and complete Liubo sets from royal mausoleums, aristocratic burials and Han Dynasty tombs across China. Museums, including the Metropolitan Museum of Art, preserve these remarkable artefacts. Paintings, stone reliefs and funerary objects even depict people gathered around Liubo boards, confirming that it was far more than an obscure pastime.A carved board inside a Han Dynasty tomb or a complete gaming set recovered from an ancient burial may appear modest compared with spectacular treasures of gold or jade, yet each provides another clue about a game that dominated Chinese society for centuries before disappearing almost completely by the end of the Tang Dynasty. Future excavations may eventually uncover an illustrated manual, an inscribed game board or a more detailed written account capable of solving the mystery.Until then, Liubo remains one of archaeology's most intriguing unsolved puzzles. It is a rare example of a game whose equipment, artwork and cultural significance have survived for more than two millennia, while the knowledge required to play it has quietly slipped out of history.
Article Summary: Rare Liubo game boards discovered inside Han Dynasty tombs. Archaeologists identified two Liubos engraved directly onto square bricks. The discovery formed part of a larger excavation that also revealed pottery figurines, ceramic vessels and other funerary objects. The find highlights the game's importance in everyday life.

Article Title: 4 held for theft of 17 kg silver mask, cladding of Shivling at historic temple in Maharashtra's Khopoli
Article Text:

NAVI MUMBAI: The Khopoli police in Raigad detected the burglary at the 18th century historic Shree Vireshwar temple, where 17 kg silver mask and silver cladding on Shivling was stolen on July 19 past midnight around 2 am, by arresting four accused burglars on Tuesday.The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe (36) and Vikas Agiwale (25), who were arrested from Shirur, Pune district and Dilip Jadhav (40) and Sakharam Gaikwad (40), who were arrested from Parner in Ahilyanagar district.The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust from the donations received from devotees.Sachin Hire, senior inspector of Khopoli said, "On July 19, the assistant priest at the temple identified as Kishore Shigwan (56) lodge a complaint that the silver mask and cladding on Shivling was stolen. The thieves had entered the temple by breaking the chain and lock of the rear gate, which always remained close as the devotees were allowed entry only from the front gate.""Upon checking CCTV camera footage at the temple, it was seen that four masked men had entered the sanctum sanctorum around 2 am and decamped with the silver mask and cladding on the Shivling. Subsequently, an FIR was registered under BNS sections for house tres-pass, theft in a dwelling house and joint criminal liability. "Inspector Hire said, "Multiple teams were formed to trace the gang of burglars.Using technical expertise and informer network, we zeroed-in on four history-sheeters. They were traced to Pune and Ahilyanagar district and gradually apprehended on Tuesday.""They have revealed the place where they have hidden the stolen silver mask and cladding. Accordingly, a police team will recover the stolen valuables. Previously, there are criminal cases of theft and robbery registered against the arrested accused in Ahilyanagar and Pune districts."
Article Summary: The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust. The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe, Vikas Agiwale, Dilip Jadhav and Sakharam Gaikwad.

We are retrieving more CCTV footages from other shops in our building for providing them to Ulwe police."PSI Rama Dhavare of Ulwe said, "After registering an FIR, the forensic team collected the human semen sample and hair strands from the crime scene. Once the accused is arrested, the DNA match will be the vital evidence in court for conviction of the accused."
Article Summary: The incident occurred outside a tea shop on the ground floor in Siddhivinayak Platinum society in sector 23, Ulwe on Sunday around 11.45pm. The unidentified accused was booked under BNS section and Prevention of Cruelty to Animal.

Article Title: 9 woman rescued from flesh trade in Taloja lodge, 3 accused held
Article Text:
The crime branch team arrested three accused including the lodge manager and two waiters.

NAVI MUMBAI: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) of Navi Mumbai crime branch busted a prostitution racket at hotel-cum lodge in Taloja and rescued nine women from the flesh trade on July 18. The crime branch team arrested three accused including the lodge manager and two waiters.Gajanan Kadam, senior inspector of AHTU said, "As per the information received about prostitution being carried out at Hotel Abode Inn Lodging and Boarding in Taloja, we set a trap by sending a decoy customer, whom the lodge manager provided a woman for sexual favour for Rs 3,000 that was accepted by one waiter. On the signal of the customer customer, we raided the lodge, where 9 women were kept for prostitution. The lodge manager Balram Gowda, waiters Girish Pujari and Krishnaraj Patil were arrested for dragging the women into prostitution. An FIR was registered at Taloja police station against the three arrested accused Gowda, Pujari and Patil, who were booked relevant BNS sections and Prevention of Immoral Trafficking Act. The Panvel court remanded them to police custody till July 21. The rescued women were sent to women's shelter home as directed by the magistrate."
Article Summary: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit of Navi Mumbai crime branch busted a prostitution racket at hotel-cum lodge in Taloja. The crime branch team arrested three accused including the lodge manager and two waiters. The lodge manager Balram Gowda, waiters Girish Pujari and Krishnaraj Patil were arrested.

Article Title: Truck driver arrested from Gujarat for killing fellow driver with iron rod over caste dispute in Maharashtra
Article Text:
Taloja police have caught a truck driver involved in the tragic murder of a fellow driver during a dispute fueled by caste discrimination (Representative image)

NAVI MUMBAI: Taloja police have arrested a 40-year-old truck driver who had absconded after fatally assaulting a 45-year-old truck driver on his head with an iron rod in the truck parking lot of Nisha Transport company in Nitlas village near Taloja industrial area in Panvel taluka on July 14 early morning.The accused was arrested from Valsad railway station, Gujarat on Friday, while he was escaping by train to his home town in UP.The arrested accused has been identified as Ramesh Kumar Yadav and the murder victim as Chandan Pandey, both hailing from UP.Sagar Nikam, PI (crime) of Taloja said, "The murder was an outcome of the Pandey versus Yadav caste discrimination, especially in UP. The accused Yadav had fatally assaulted the victim Pandey as the latter being a Brahmin used to humiliate Yadav from OBC by treating him as inferior, as claimed by the accused Yadav."PI Nikam informed, "On Monday night, an argument has ensued between Pandey and Yadav in the parking lot over caste discrimination. As they quarrelled, the other truck drivers intervened and resolved the matter. On Tuesday around 5.30 am, again both of them quarrelled, when Yadav assaulted on Pandey's head with an iron rod that proved fatal.""Pandey escaped after threatening other truckers if they attempted to catch him. The security guard Mohammad Alam Hajif-ul Khan (58) informed the police. Pandey was rushed to Panvel sub-district hospital where he was declared brought dead. Subsequently, a murder case was registered against the accused Yadav. His photograph found in his parked truck was immediately circulated to the GRP and RPF at railway stations where multiple trains heading to UP halt.""On Friday, the Valsad GRP informed us that Yadav has been detained at Valsad railway station while he was travelling in an express train to escape to his hometown in UP. Our police team reached Valsad and arrested Yadav. The Panvel JMFC court has remanded Yadav to police custody untill July 21."
Article Summary: Ramesh Kumar Yadav, 40, was arrested from Valsad railway station, Gujarat on Friday. He had absconded after fatally assaulting a 45-year-old truck driver on his head with an iron rod. The murder was an outcome of the Pandey versus Yadav caste discrimination, especially in UP.

Article Title: Rag picker's murder detected within 24 hours, accused arrested from Bhiwandi
Article Text:
Rag picker's murder detected within 24 hours, accused arrested from Bhiwandi (Representational Image)

NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai crime branch unit-2 team has arrested a murder accused from Bhiwandi while conducting a parallel probe in the murder case registered at NRI Coastal police station on Friday after an unidentified man's body with head injuries was found on the pavement near D-Mart in sector 15, Belapur on Friday around 1 am.The arrested accused has been identified as Mohammad Irfan Mohammed Husain Ansari (36) and the murder victim as Salman Anwar Shaikh (27), a resident of Govandi. Both working as rag pickers for livelihood.Anil Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-2 informed that, during the probe, when inquired with some rag pickers in the locality, we got an eye witness, who knew Ansari and had seen him assaulting Shaikh with a wooden stick on Thursday night as a quarrel broke out between them after they together consumed liquor near the pavement.The eye witness told that Ansari would pick up rags during day and would spend night where ever he found empty gala or incomplete under construction bldg in Belapur and his father resided in Bhiwandi.Using technical expertise and informer network Ansari was apprehended from Bhiwandi within 24 hours. Thereafter, the murder victim's identity was revealed by him.SPI Patil said, "Ansari claimed that Shaikh was habitual of abusing others after getting drunk. On Thursday night, after the liquor session, Shaikh turned violent without being provoked and attempted to assault him with an iron rod after pushing him to the ground. Hence, he confronted Shaikh by assaulting him with a wooden stick on his head. Seeing Shaikh bleeding profusely and fallen unconscious, he escaped to Bhiwandi. "
Article Summary: Rag picker's murder detected within 24 hours, accused arrested from Bhiwandi. Mohammad Irfan Mohammed Husain Ansari (36) and the murder victim as Salman Anwar Shaikh (27), a resident of Govandi. Both working as rag pickers for livelihood.

Article Title: Cash of ₹8.06 lakh robbed by four men using pepper spray
Article Text:
Representative image

Pune:





Four men riding a motorcycle robbed a liquor shop cashier of Rs 8.06 lakh after spraying pepper on his face around 10.55 pm on Sunday.The cashier, Hauskumar Ingale (42) of Narhe, lodged a complaint with the Narhe police on Monday morning. Inspector Ishwar Chavan said, “The incident took place on the service road of the Katraj-Dehu Road bypass near Prayeja City. Ingale was on his way to Dange Chowk in Pimpri Chinchwad to deliver the cash to a bar. The money was kept in the scooter’s storage compartment when the four assailants intercepted him, sprayed pepper on his face, robbed him of the cash, and threatened him with dire consequences before fleeing.”This was the second such robbery involving the liquor shop’s cash. “On April 12 this year, Rs 4 lakh being transported from the same liquor shop was robbed near Navale Bridge. Police later arrested two suspects in that case,” he added.“We are examining CCTV footage from the service road and the Katraj-Dehu Road bypass to identify the suspects and ascertain the registration number of the motorcycle,” Chavan said.
Article Summary: The cashier, Hauskumar Ingale (42) of Narhe, lodged a complaint with the Narhe police on Monday morning. Ingale was on his way to Dange Chowk in Pimpri Chinchwad to deliver the cash to a bar.

Article Title: Loadman-turned-officer offers free coaching for TN civil service aspirants
Article Text:
P Manimaran with his students





MADURAI: P Manimaran seldom took a break on weekends when he was preparing for TNPSC, between shifts transporting heavy sacks as a loadman. After cracking the exam and becoming a revenue inspector he still doesn’t relax on weekends. Instead, he spends his Saturdays and Sundays coaching civil service aspirants for free, to ensure that lack of money or guidance does not stand between poor students and a govt job.The senior revenue inspector, who worked as a loadman from Class X until completing his MPhil, runs two coaching centres named after former President Abdul Kalam at Alwarpuram in Madurai and another centre at Tharaikudi in Ramanathapuram district. Both centres conduct classes and mock tests without charging students every weekend.Manimaran, son of a daily wage labourer in Alwarpuram, was never deterred by the financial struggle at home. Despite challenges he completed his post-graduation and subsequently MPhil too. But finding the right job proved elusive forcing him to work as a loadman.He entered govt service as a village administrative officer in 2015 and later became a senior revenue inspector.The govt job transformed his life. That’s when Manimaran decided to enable other poor students too to aspire for what he had achieved. In 2018, he began creating awareness among youth in his neighbourhood about govt examinations and started teaching them on weekends.“I didn’t even know that clearing the TNPSC examination was required to secure a govt job. A friend helped me begin preparing on weekends while I was working as a loadman. So I want to help others,” he said.Manimaran said families with money could send their children to private coaching institutes, while others were often left without guidance. “My education helped improve my family’s circumstances, but many others facing the same struggles still have no one to guide them,” he said.After being posted in Ramanathapuram district, he opened the Tharaikudi centre in 2022 at the Panchayat Union Middle School. The Alwarpuram centre was opened subsequently at Thirupathi Venkatachalapathy Primary School.“I was clueless about TNPSC. It was because of this centre, I got to know about this exam, and how to crack it,’’ says R Vasantha Kumar of Alwarpuram, who has now become a junior assistant in the state animal husbandry department. Vasantha Kumar now volunteers to coach other students.So far, more than 1,000 youth have been trained at the centres out of which 33 have cleared Group II and Group IV examinations. “We provide guidance on past years’ question papers, strategies for facing the exam, and the specific topics from which questions are likely to be asked,” he said.Former students who secured govt jobs now return to teach current batches. The centres are also preparing to introduce coaching for UPSC and Group I examinations.For aspirants outside Madurai and Ramanathapuram, the team runs Telegram and YouTube channels under the name ‘Tharaikudi TNPSC Free Coaching Centre’. Videos posted on these platforms receive an average of 1,000 to 2,000 views.
Article Summary: P Manimaran runs two coaching centres named after former President Abdul Kalam at Alwarpuram in Madurai and another centre at Tharaikudi in Ramanathapuram district. Both centres conduct classes and mock tests without charging students every weekend. More than 1,000 youth have been trained at the centres.
